questions.q: What data source does a Financial Reporting Studio report query against?
options: The raw General Ledger transactional tables directly
A pre-summarized, multidimensional GL balances cube
A flat CSV export of journal entries
An external data warehouse unrelated to Oracle Fusion
questions.explain: Financial Reporting Studio reports are built against a GL balances cube, a multidimensional summary structure built from posted balances.

questions.q: In a typical Financial Reporting Studio grid, what do rows usually represent?
options: The point of view being compared, like periods or scenarios
What you're reporting on — individual accounts, ranges, or summary lines
The user's security role
The export file format
questions.explain: Rows typically represent the accounts, account ranges, or summary lines (like Total Revenue) being reported on.

questions.q: In a typical Financial Reporting Studio grid, what do columns usually represent?
options: The point of view being compared across, such as periods or Actual vs. Budget
The specific GL account numbers
The report's file name
The data security policy applied
questions.explain: Columns commonly represent periods or scenarios being compared side by side, letting a reader scan for trends or variances.

questions.q: Why does referencing an account hierarchy's parent node (rather than listing child accounts individually) matter for a row definition?
options: It has no practical effect either way
A hierarchy-based row automatically rolls up new child accounts added later; a row listing accounts individually can silently miss them
Hierarchy-based rows are always slower to calculate
Only formulas can reference hierarchies
questions.explain: A parent node in an account hierarchy automatically includes its children, so the report stays accurate as the chart of accounts evolves.

questions.q: What is a "formula row" in a Financial Reporting Studio report, such as a Gross Margin row?
options: A row that pulls a balance directly from the cube like any other row
A row that computes its result from other rows already on the report, rather than pulling a balance from the cube
A row that can only exist in BI Publisher, not Financial Reporting Studio
A row reserved exclusively for currency conversion
questions.explain: A formula row, such as Gross Margin = Total Revenue - Total COGS, calculates its value from other rows rather than referencing the cube directly.
